text:
Nashville is 8-2-0 in its last ten and sits at 13-6-5, a .650 points percentage that would have sounded like a joke in October. Some of that is real. Our numbers have the Predators even on expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets) at 50.4%, and 52% over the last ten. The rest is the goaltending: they have allowed nine fewer goals than their chances against would predict, and by our count they have about 4.4 more points than their play deserved.

The trade that changed the look of the roster came on Nov. 1, when Nashville sent Matthew Wood to Seattle for Shane Wright. Wright has landed on a line with Filip Forsberg and Nils Hoglander that has outscored opponents 10-4 at five on five with a 55% share of the chances. That is the line to watch. Jonathan Marchessault has three points in two games since coming back from injury, and Roman Josi and Adam Wilsby have been the best pair on the team by chance share.

The worry is the older center group. Steven Stamkos, Ryan O'Reilly and Mavrik Bourque have been outscored 11-6 together, and O'Reilly's name keeps turning up in trade chatter. Our playoff odds sit at 67%. That is a good place to be, but the cushion was built partly on saves, and saves are the least reliable thing in hockey.
headline: The Predators are winning more than their chances say
